genes/CAUVC/imuA/imuA-ai-review.yaml.description: ImuA (CC_3213) is the first gene of the SOS-regulated imuA-imuB-dnaE2 operon of Caulobacter crescentus. Deletion of imuA makes cells extremely sensitive to mitomycin C and strongly reduces UV- and mitomycin C-induced mutagenesis, the same phenotype as deletion of imuB or dnaE2, placing all three products in one damage-tolerance pathway that performs error-prone synthesis across DNA lesions. ImuA has a RecA-like P-loop fold but no demonstrated catalytic or DNA-binding activity of its own; it is an accessory component rather than the polymerase of the cassette.

review.summary: The imuA promoter is one of the experimentally confirmed LexA-dependent promoters of the C. crescentus SOS regulon.
review.reason: Correct, and the induction gate is real, but SOS regulon membership is the regulatory context rather than what the protein does; error-prone translesion synthesis is the effector process and is annotated separately in this review.

which was confirmed by site-directed mutagenesis studies of the imuA promoter

review.summary: An in-frame imuA deletion abolishes mitomycin C-induced mutagenesis and strongly reduces UV-induced mutagenesis while sensitizing cells to both agents, and the phenotype is complemented by the wild-type allele.
review.reason: The deletion genetics establish participation in damage tolerance whose output is induced mutation, which is what error-prone translesion synthesis describes; single imuA, imuB and dnaE2 mutants share the phenotype and imuB dnaE2 double mutants are not additive, so the three products act in one lesion-bypass pathway. The experiments were done in NA1000, a derivative of the sequenced CB15 strain this entry represents, which is also how GOA assigns PMID:18083815 to this accession.

supported_by.supporting_text: The genes imuA and imuB encode previously uncharacterized proteins, which are shown here for the first time to be involved in DNA damage tolerance.
The single mutants imuA, imuB and dnaE2 mutants are extremely sensitive to this condition, revealing that this operon plays a major role in the tolerance to the mit C-induced DNA lesions.
Both the UV and the mit C sensitivity phenotypes of imuA could be complemented by vector pMR3213, containing the wild-type imuA allele.

Altogether, the results shown in Figure 6 demonstrate that the imuAB dnaE2 operon is involved in mutagenic repair of UV lesions, and suggest that the proteins encoded by this operon cooperate in the same pathway, as evidenced by the similar phenotypes of the single mutants, and by the epistatic effect of imuB and dnaE2 mutations.

knowledge_gaps.gap_statement: No molecular activity has been demonstrated for ImuA: whether it binds DNA, binds ImuB directly, or has a nucleotide-dependent activity is unknown.

genes/CAUVC/imuB/imuB-ai-review.yaml.description: ImuB (CC_3212) is the middle gene of the SOS-regulated imuA-imuB-dnaE2 operon of Caulobacter crescentus. It carries a UmuC/Y-family polymerase fold but, like other ImuB proteins, lacks the active-site carboxylates needed for catalysis, and in the characterized mycobacterial cassette it works as a polymerase-inactive adaptor that binds ImuA, DnaE2 and the beta clamp. Deletion of C. crescentus imuB sensitizes cells to UV and mitomycin C and changes the UV mutational spectrum in the same way as deletion of dnaE2, without additivity in the double mutant, so ImuB and DnaE2 act in one lesion-bypass pathway distinct from the E. coli umuDC system.

review.summary: Correct in direction but far broader than the evidence: ImuB does not repair lesions, it supports synthesis past them.
review.reason: The row is a UniProt combined-pipeline IEA whose stated basis is the UmuC domain IPR001126 plus the TreeGrafter node PANTHER:PTN000118183, neither of which resolves beyond generic DNA repair; it is not a PAINT IBA. The C. crescentus deletion experiments show lesion tolerance with induced mutagenesis, not lesion removal, so error-prone translesion synthesis is the term the evidence supports; it sits under DNA damage tolerance rather than under DNA repair.

supported_by.supporting_text: These results indicate that imuB and dnaE2 cooperate in a lesion bypass pathway, which has a different specificity than that involving umuDC in E.coli.

review.summary: An imuB deletion is extremely sensitive to mitomycin C, loses most UV-induced mutagenesis, and shifts the surviving UV mutational spectrum exactly as a dnaE2 deletion does.
review.reason: Deletion, epistasis with dnaE2 and the shared change in mutational signature establish participation in damage-tolerant synthesis whose output is induced mutation. The mutational-spectrum result is direct evidence that the pathway inserts nucleotides opposite lesions rather than removing them.

supported_by.supporting_text: The imuB dnaE2 double mutant does not exhibit an exacerbated phenotype, indicating again that these genes cooperate in the same pathway of damage tolerance.
The mutation signature of UV light is remarkably similar in dnaE2 and imuB strains.
This novel mutational signature, dependent on the activity of the imuAB/dnaE2 operon, probably reflects a difference in polymerase preference for nucleotide incorporation during TLS.

review.summary: ImuB is a noncatalytic interaction hub: the characterized mycobacterial ortholog binds ImuA, DnaE2 and the beta clamp, and losing the clamp interaction alone destroys cassette function.
review.reason: The adaptor activity is transferred from the mycobacterial ortholog, where it rests on two-hybrid interactions plus a separation-of-function clamp-binding allele, and the same paper states that ImuB homologs generally lack the catalytic residues, so the fold cannot be read as polymerase activity. C. crescentus ImuB keeps the UmuC fold and the genetic requirement, so the role transfers, but the interactions have not been tested in this organism.

supported_by.supporting_text: Yeast two-hybrid analyses indicate that ImuB interacts with both ImuA' and DnaE2, as well as with the beta-clamp.
Despite retaining structural features characteristic of Y-family members, ImuB homologs lack conserved active-site amino acids required for polymerase activity.

genes/CAUVC/dnaE2/dnaE2-ai-review.yaml.description: DnaE2 (CC_3211) is the DNA polymerase of the SOS-regulated imuA-imuB-dnaE2 operon of Caulobacter crescentus and a member of the DnaE2 subfamily of type-C polymerases, distinct from the essential replicative alpha subunit DnaE. Deletion of dnaE2 makes cells extremely sensitive to mitomycin C, abolishes mitomycin C-induced mutagenesis and strongly reduces UV-induced mutagenesis, with a characteristic change in the UV mutational spectrum shared with the imuB mutant; the imuB dnaE2 double mutant is no worse than either single mutant. DnaE2 therefore supplies the nucleotide-insertion step of error-prone synthesis across lesions, acting with the ImuA and ImuB accessory proteins rather than in chromosome replication.

review.summary: Template binding is intrinsic to a DNA polymerase, but the term is very broad.
review.reason: True but less specific than the evidence supports, and not an ancestor of the activity asserted as core: GO:0003887 has no is_a path to GO:0003676, so this is a refinement rather than a TOO_GENERAL case. The row is mapped from a generic nucleic-acid-binding domain signature, but this protein's curated activity is DNA-templated synthesis on a DNA primer-template, so DNA binding is the supported child term.

review.summary: Catalytic activity is true but uninformative.
review.reason: True of the protein but uninformative: GO:0003887, accepted in this review, is an is_a descendant of catalytic activity and so already entails it. The claim is not wrong, which is why this is TOO_GENERAL rather than an over-annotation.

review.summary: This is the defining catalytic activity of DnaE2.
review.reason: UniProt places Q9A3J3 in the DnaE2 subfamily of type-C DNA polymerases and records the templated nucleotidyl-transfer reaction; in the characterized mycobacterial cassette, substituting the DnaE2 catalytic residues reproduces the deletion phenotype, which establishes that the DnaE2 alpha subunit, and not ImuB, performs the synthesis. The purified C. crescentus enzyme has not been assayed, so the activity rests on the family assignment plus the ortholog catalytic-residue result.

In contrast, replacement of DnaE2 catalytic residues reproduces the dnaE2 gene deletion phenotype, strongly implying a direct role for the α-subunit in mutagenic lesion bypass.

review.reason: Correct and as precise as a bacterial cytoplasmic protein can be annotated, but it is inherited from the UniRule subcellular-location line rather than measured here, and it is not what the gene is for.

review.summary: This term conflates DnaE2 with the essential replicative alpha subunit it is paralogous to.
review.reason: The mapping comes from the shared DNA polymerase III alpha domains (IPR004805, IPR011708). DnaE2 is dispensable for growth, induced only on damage, and lacks the C-terminal region through which the replicative alpha subunit engages the clamp loader, so it cannot substitute for replicative synthesis; damage-induced lesion bypass is the real process.

supported_by.supporting_text: All major DNA polymerase IIIα structural/functional domains ( 23 , 24 ) are readily identified in DnaE2, except for the very C-terminal region which in E. coli has been implicated in the interaction of α with the clamp-loader subunit, τ ( 28 , 29 ).
DnaE2 orthologs clearly form a distinct branch, including the DnaE2 from C.crescentus.

review.summary: Broad DNA repair does not capture what the deletion experiments show, which is mutagenic bypass rather than lesion removal.
review.reason: The row is a UniRule transfer. The C. crescentus genetics show that dnaE2 loss abolishes induced mutagenesis while sensitizing cells to the damaging agent, which is damage tolerance with an error-prone outcome; error-prone translesion synthesis is the specific supported term and is annotated from the primary data in this review.

supported_by.supporting_text: These results indicate that imuB and dnaE2 cooperate in a lesion bypass pathway, which has a different specificity than that involving umuDC in E.coli.

review.summary: DnaE2 is induced by DNA damage and acts on damaged templates.
review.reason: True, and the induction is real: the operon is upregulated after UV and mitomycin C in a recA-dependent way. But GO:0042276, asserted in this review, is an is_a descendant of DNA damage response through GO:0019985 and GO:0006301, so this term adds nothing beyond it.

supported_by.supporting_text: The results shown in Figure 5 demonstrate that imuA, imuB and dnaE2 expression levels are increased similarly in response to UV damage.

review.summary: Proofreading chemistry is mapped from domains shared with the replicative polymerase, but DnaE2 proteins have lost the residues that carry it.
review.reason: The term comes from the generic DnaE/PHP domain mappings IPR004805 and IPR011708. Published comparison of the PHP domains shows that the replicative DnaE1 retains the exonuclease residues whereas they are absent in DnaE2, and a proofreading activity would also sit awkwardly with the error-prone role established genetically. No exonuclease assay exists for any DnaE2, so the activity is not asserted here as absent, only as unsupported.

supported_by.supporting_text: The corresponding domain of Mtb DnaE1 retains all amino acids associated with exonuclease activity ( 34 – 36 ), whereas key residues are absent in DnaE2.

review.summary: The parent polymerase term is valid but redundant with its DNA-directed child.

review.summary: A dnaE2 disruption abolishes mitomycin C-induced mutagenesis, reduces UV-induced mutagenesis and changes the UV mutational spectrum, in the same pathway as imuB.
review.reason: This is the process the primary C. crescentus data establish: the mutational-signature change shows that the pathway inserts nucleotides opposite lesions, the sensitivity shows tolerance, and the epistasis with imuB shows one pathway. DnaE2 supplies the catalytic step, so the annotation is direct rather than regulatory.

supported_by.supporting_text: The results show that the dnaE2 operon is upregulated in response to DNA damage in a recA-dependent manner, and demonstrate that all three genes that compose this expression unit are involved in UV and mitomycin C-induced mutagenesis.
This novel mutational signature, dependent on the activity of the imuAB/dnaE2 operon, probably reflects a difference in polymerase preference for nucleotide incorporation during TLS.
In combination with the prediction that ImuB lacks polymerase activity, this observation implies that DnaE2 catalyzes translesion synthesis.
